name: yearbind
description: Yearbind makes a group yearbook for a class, reunion, team or club. The organizer starts it in ChatGPT; members join by link with no account, add a photo and a quote, and vote on kind superlatives. Retro yearbook portraits come from ChatGPT's own image tools. The finished book can be previewed page by page and, in the United States and Canada, ordered by adults as a printed hardcover.

interface.longDescription:
Yearbind is a yearbook maker for reunions, school classes, sports teams, clubs and any other group: one yearbook your whole group makes together.

Start it in ChatGPT and you get one join link. Everyone opens it on their phone or computer, with no account, and adds a photo, their name and a short quote. You approve each person before the others see them.

Retro portraits: share a photo and ask ChatGPT for a 1970s, 1980s, 1990s or 2000s yearbook portrait. ChatGPT makes the image and Yearbind puts it in the book under the name you give. Pick an era look for the whole book and every photo gets the same treatment, so phone selfies and ChatGPT portraits sit together.

Kind superlatives: members vote from their own page on titles like Most likely to start a business or Biggest heart. Superlatives are positive only and never about looks, bodies or dating. Nobody sees vote counts; when you close voting, Yearbind reveals only the winners.

The finished book has a title page, member pages with portraits and quotes, the superlative winners and signature pages, laid out as an 8.5 x 11 inch book you can preview page by page.

In the United States and Canada, the finished book can also be ordered as a hardcover: once voting is closed, the organizer and every member aged 18 or over can order it. Checkout happens on yearbind.ambientapp.ai, never in ChatGPT: the buyer enters the delivery address, confirms they are 18 or older and pays there. Printed copies ship only to the United States and Canada; in every other country Yearbind works the same, without printed copies.

Details:
- Members need no ChatGPT and no account; their personal link lets them change their entry, vote or remove themselves at any time.
- Every photo and every word is checked before it is shown, and the organizer approves each member.
- For ages 13 and up. Where printed copies are offered, only adults 18 and over can order them; a parent or guardian can order for a younger member.
capabilities: Start a yearbook your group joins from one link
Add retro yearbook photos from ChatGPT
Preview the finished book page by page
defaultPrompt: Make a 90s-style yearbook for our 20-year reunion
Make an end-of-season yearbook for my soccer team, as a gift for our coach
Add kind superlatives to our yearbook

positive.description: Start a yearbook. Run this first, in a new chat, with Yearbind picked: type @Yearbook, choose Yearbook Maker for Reunions, then type the prompt (Try in chat on the plugin's page does the same). Without it ChatGPT may answer on its own instead of using Yearbind; if a later case gets the reply that Yearbind isn't available, pick it again the same way. There is nothing to sign in to: each ChatGPT user gets their own yearbooks. ChatGPT may show its own 'Allow ChatGPT to use Yearbook Maker for Reunions?' prompt first (the join link is a page anyone with the link can open); choose Allow once. The case passes with or without it. ChatGPT may open the card in a side panel; the panel shows the same card.
positive.prompt: Use Yearbind to start a yearbook for the Lincoln High class of 2016 ten-year reunion. I'm Dana Reyes.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the yearbook. The card shows 'Lincoln High class of 2016' (or the title ChatGPT chose), the join link yearbind.ambientapp.ai/j/ followed by an 8-character code, 1 member, and the buttons Open yearbook and My page. The reply gives the join link and says members need no account and the organizer approves each person. ChatGPT asks for no email, phone, address or age.

positive.description: Add a portrait from an image. Run after case 1, in the same chat. Attach the file from file_attachment_urls (a drawn yearbook-style portrait, not a real person). To try the full flow, you may instead attach any photo and ask ChatGPT first to 'make a 1990s yearbook portrait of this photo'; ChatGPT then hands its own image to Yearbind the same way.
positive.prompt: Add this as Maria Lopez's portrait in our yearbook.
positive.expected_behavior: Maria Lopez becomes a member with that portrait. The card shows her personal link to send her. The reply says Maria Lopez's portrait is in the yearbook and does not describe the image. Sending the same image again says it is already there.

positive.description: Superlatives stay kind. Run after case 1.
positive.prompt: Add the superlatives 'Most likely to start a band' and 'Best looking' to our yearbook.
positive.expected_behavior: 'Most likely to start a band' is added. 'Best looking' is refused because Yearbind superlatives are never about looks, and the reply says so. The card's Superlatives tab lists the new one. A title about style or clothes, such as 'Best dressed', is refused the same way if you try it.

positive.description: A member joins on the web. Run after case 1. Open the join link from case 1 in any browser or phone (no ChatGPT needed), type a name such as Sam Lee, tick 'I'm 13 or older' and press Join the yearbook (a photo is optional). The page then shows 'Waiting for the organizer's OK'. Then send the prompt below.
positive.prompt: Who has joined our yearbook so far?
positive.expected_behavior: The reply says how many members are in the book and that 1 person is waiting for the organizer's OK in the card, and names no one the result doesn't list. The card shows 'Review 1 waiting'; tapping it and then Approve moves Sam Lee into the yearbook.

positive.description: Close voting and order a copy. Run after case 4, from the United States or Canada: printed copies ship only there, so from another country start_order answers that printed yearbooks aren't available in your country and the card has no Order tab. Optional before it: on the member's page from case 4, choose someone for a superlative and press Save my votes. ChatGPT may ask to allow close_voting first, because closing voting can't be undone, and may ask again before start_order; choose Allow once each time. To finish checkout, open the link, use any US address, tick 'I'm 18 or older', open 'Add promotion code' in the payment form and enter the review code YEARBIND-0B7B174C (for reviewers: 100% off, at most 50 uses). The order then costs nothing, no card is needed, and it goes to our printer's test system, so nothing is printed, shipped or charged.
positive.prompt: Close voting on our yearbook, tell me the winners, then order one printed copy.
positive.expected_behavior: Voting closes and the book is final: the reply names the winner of each superlative that got enough votes (or says none did) and gives no vote counts. Then start_order returns a checkout link on yearbind.ambientapp.ai/c/; the reply says printed copies are for adults 18 and over and that nothing is charged in ChatGPT. The checkout page shows the total and asks the buyer to confirm they are 18 or older before payment. No card number or address is asked for in chat. The card shows Final and an Order tab. From outside the United States and Canada the reply says printed yearbooks aren't available in your country, with no checkout link, and the card shows Final without an Order tab.

negative.description: Writing a quote is ChatGPT's own job; no yearbook is involved.
negative.prompt: Write me a funny senior quote about loving pizza.
negative.expected_behavior: ChatGPT writes quotes itself. No Yearbind tool is called.
ChatGPT explains it itself. No Yearbind tool is called.

negative.description: Ranking people by looks is not something Yearbind does.
negative.prompt: Rank the people in my class photo from best looking to worst.
negative.expected_behavior: No Yearbind tool is called and no yearbook or superlative is created; ChatGPT answers on its own.

review.commerce_description: Sells one physical product: a printed hardcover group yearbook (8.5 x 11 in), printed and shipped by Lulu to the United States and Canada. Orders are for adults 18 and over. The plugin is listed in every country, and printing is offered only to users in the United States and Canada (the country ChatGPT reports with each call in openai/userLocation, else the region of openai/locale): everywhere else the results, the card and the members' pages of a yearbook run from there show no price, order or checkout, and start_order answers that printed yearbooks aren't available in the user's country. start_order and the card return a link to our own checkout page on yearbind.ambientapp.ai (Stripe), which asks the buyer to confirm they are 18 or older before payment; the plugin opens that page with openExternal and never collects payment or address data. Members aged 13 to 17 can be in a yearbook but can't order.

publication.release_notes: Listed in every country. Printed copies still ship only to the United States and Canada: elsewhere the results, the card and the members' pages show no order option, and start_order says printed yearbooks aren't available in that country. Listing: renamed Yearbook Maker for Reunions, with the subtitle "Classes, teams & superlatives"; keywords for yearbook makers, reunions, offices, sports teams, superlatives and AI yearbook photos; capabilities say what the yearbook does; new starter prompts and a dark-mode icon. Adds three skills: group yearbook, kind superlatives and retro yearbook photos.
